description:
Ask a workspace's own agent to merge its merge request.

This does not merge anything. It composes the request Bloom's agent-guided merge choice composes, with the project's merge instructions attached, and sends it into that workspace's chat as an ordinary message. The agent runs `glab mr merge` there, in front of the owner, under whatever permission mode they set, and can say what GitLab answered if it refuses.

So it returns once the turn has begun, and the merging happens inside that turn, after this call is over. Nothing has landed on GitLab when this answers, and the merge may still not happen. Do not report a merge request as merged on the strength of this call. Call workspace_list with include_github afterwards and read the state.

It refuses a merge request GitLab will not take, a worktree holding work GitLab has not got, and a workspace whose agent is busy. When it refuses, do not run `glab mr merge` yourself and do not ask another agent to. Merging publishes to a server other people share, and this tool only asks the workspace's own agent to do it.

Name the workspace by the id workspace_list reports, not by its name. It squash merges unless you say otherwise.

method.description: How to merge it. Leave it out for squash, which is what Bloom's own button proposes.

workspace.description: The workspace whose merge request to merge, by the id workspace_list reports. Not its name: two workspaces may share one.

name: workspace_merge
